patches.rationale: merge_config currently does a shallow dict update, so nested mappings are replaced wholesale and nested objects are shared with the inputs. The fix implements a recursive merge: when both base and overrides hold mappings at the same key, recurse; otherwise the override value wins (lists included, replaced not concatenated). To guarantee independence, every value placed into the result is deep-copied, so neither input is mutated and no nested mutable object is shared with either input. Simple non-nested overrides keep their existing behavior. New regression tests in tests/test_merge_config_regression.py cover nested merge, leaf precedence, base-only/override-only keys, list replacement, input non-mutation, and output independence.

edits.old:
def merge_config(defaults, overrides):
    result = dict(defaults)
    result.update(overrides)
    return result

contract_tests: merge_config(base, overrides) returns a mapping containing all keys from base and overrides -> test_keys_only_in_base_are_preserved and test_keys_only_in_overrides_are_added assert exact dict equality including both key sets.

For keys present in both inputs where both values are mappings, the result contains a recursive merge of the two mappings -> test_nested_mapping_is_merged_recursively asserts result == {'db': {'host': 'localhost', 'port': 5433, 'opts': {'ssl': True}}}, preserving base-only nested keys while applying nested overrides.
At leaf keys, the value from overrides wins over the value from base -> test_leaf_override_wins asserts result['a']['b'] == 2 (int) from overrides.
Keys only present in base are preserved in the result -> test_keys_only_in_base_are_preserved asserts result == {'a': 1, 'b': 3}.
Keys only present in overrides are added to the result -> test_keys_only_in_overrides_are_added asserts result == {'a': 1, 'b': 2}.

List values are replaced by the overrides list, not concatenated with the base list -> test_lists_are_replaced_not_concatenated asserts result['items'] == [4, 5] and test_nested_lists_are_replaced_not_concatenated asserts result['cfg']['items'] == [3].
merge_config does not mutate the base input mapping or any of its nested objects -> test_base_input_is_not_mutated asserts base == base_snapshot after the call.
merge_config does not mutate the overrides input mapping or any of its nested objects -> test_overrides_input_is_not_mutated asserts overrides == overrides_snapshot after the call.

The returned mapping does not share nested mutable objects with base or overrides; mutating the result does not affect either input -> test_result_does_not_share_nested_objects_with_base and test_result_does_not_share_nested_objects_with_overrides mutate result nested dicts/lists and assert inputs unchanged; test_returned_lists_are_independent_copies asserts identity inequality and post-mutation input stability.
Simple (non-nested) overrides continue to behave as before -> test_simple_override_preserved asserts merge_config({'a': 1}, {'a': 2, 'b': 3}) == {'a': 2, 'b': 3} and merge_config({}, {}) == {}.
Returned value is a new independent mapping object -> test_returned_mapping_is_a_new_object asserts result is not base, result is not overrides, and isinstance(result, dict).
